trace_format.description: DSPy four-module pipeline trace with three external BM25 retrieval events interleaved. Each module appears as a system message declaring its signature, a user message with its inputs, and an assistant message with its outputs. 'RETRIEVAL EVENT' user messages are produced by the harness, not by an LLM. The final assistant message is a harness-assembled concatenation of every retrieved document, not a generated answer.

key_fields.description: hop-1 summary written by summarize1 from the hop-1 passages
the hop-1 summary as consumed downstream
the retrieval query written for the next hop
hop-2 summary written by summarize2 from claim, prior context and hop-2 passages
each module's reasoning before its output field

architecture.topology_details: retrieve_hop1 (harness) -> summarize1 -> create_query_hop2 -> retrieve_hop2 (harness) -> summarize2 -> create_query_hop3 -> retrieve_hop3 (harness). Four LLM modules around three retrievals. Retrieval is an external harness step, never an agent. The program's output is the union of documents returned by the three hops; no module writes an answer. Manually specified; not inferred.
architecture.verification_details: No module checks another module's output. Each consumes the previous output as given, and nothing re-reads the retrieved passages to confirm a summary preserved what the claim needs.

critical_handoffs.what_is_passed: hop-1 passages, retrieved using the claim itself
critical_handoffs.failure_risk: the candidate does not author the hop-1 query, so a hop-1 miss is not itself a candidate act; what is attributable is whether hops 2 and 3 recover from it
a summary that drops an entity the claim depends on makes the gap invisible to every later hop; the passages are not re-read
a query restating what hop 1 already retrieved spends the hop and returns nothing new
summarizing around the retrieved evidence rather than from it
the last chance to name the still-missing entity; a query aimed at an already-retrieved fact ends the run short of the required documents

summarizer.purpose: Compress retrieved passages into a summary that preserves what the claim still needs verified
summarizer.definition: Reads the claim and the passages just retrieved (and, at hop 2, the prior summary) and writes a summary that every later module depends on entirely. The passages are never re-read, so anything the summary drops is unrecoverable.
summarizer.key_behavior: Produces summary_1 / summary_2 from retrieved documents.

query_generator.purpose: Write the next retrieval query so the hop reaches a required document not yet retrieved
query_generator.definition: Reads the claim and the summaries so far and must identify which supporting entity is still missing, producing a query that targets it. There are only two authored queries in the whole run, so each one spent on an already-retrieved fact is a hop the program cannot get back.
query_generator.key_behavior: Produces the query consumed by the next external BM25 retrieval.
